title: It All Started with a Mouse
theme: Walt Disney, Mickey's origins, Oswald, early shorts and Disneyland's 1955 opening
intro: [excited] Grab your straw boater and whistle a happy tune, because tonight IT ALL STARTED WITH A MOUSE! We are going way back to Walt, the early shorts, a lucky rabbit and opening day at Disneyland. [chuckles] Black and white answers only... just kidding.

art.prompt: Wide 16:9 title card: a vintage 1920s animation desk under a warm lamp, pencil sketches pinned to the wall, a reel of nitrate film, an old riverboat steam whistle, and through the window a glowing pink fairy-tale castle and a 1950s amusement park at dusk, sepia fading into Technicolor No people, no recognizable characters, no text or logos.

categories.title: Steamboat Willie and Friends
categories.intro: [excited] Our film category is all about the cartoon shorts that started it all. Toot toot! All aboard.

art.prompt: 16:9 card art: a tiny paddle steamboat puffing round smoke rings on a black-and-white river, a hand-cranked film projector and a gramophone on a wooden dock, vintage cartoon style fading to color No people, no recognizable characters, no text or logos.

clues.clue: In the 1928 cartoon Steamboat Willie, Mickey is at the wheel of this kind of vehicle.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is a steamboat! [laughs] It is right there in the title, folks. Mickey whistles while he steers, and a legend is born.

clues.clue: This mouse, Mickey's sweetheart, also appears in Steamboat Willie, playing music with the farm animals.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Minnie Mouse. She was there from the very beginning, and she has been stealing scenes ever since.

clues.clue: Disney's musical cartoon series that began in 1929 with The Skeleton Dance.
clues.reveal: [chuckles] The correct answer is Silly Symphonies. Dancing skeletons in 1929! Walt was doing spooky season before it was cool.

clues.clue: The 1932 Silly Symphony Flowers and Trees was the first commercially released cartoon in full three-strip form of this color process.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Technicolor. And Flowers and Trees won the very first Academy Award for an animated short. [excited] Trees, you love to see it.

clues.clue: Mickey's first cartoon, test screened in 1928 as a silent short, has him copying aviator Charles Lindbergh.
clues.reveal: [gasps] The correct answer is Plane Crazy! It was made first, but Steamboat Willie, with its synchronized sound, got released first. Talk about a plot twist.

categories.title: Lucky Rabbit's Foot
categories.intro: [mischievously] This category hops through the people, and the rabbit, behind the birth of the Disney studio. Rub that lucky foot.

art.prompt: 16:9 card art: a 1920s cartoon studio storefront at twilight with a rabbit-ear shaped shadow on the window, inkwells, a rabbit's foot charm on a desk beside a film canister, warm vintage palette No people, no recognizable characters, no text or logos.

clues.clue: Walt Disney himself provided the original voice of this famous character.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Mickey Mouse. Walt voiced Mickey until 1947. [laughs] Hot dog!

clues.clue: Before Mickey, Walt created this 'Lucky Rabbit' in 1927.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Oswald the Lucky Rabbit. Walt lost the rights to him, and that heartbreak led straight to a mouse. [sighs] Unlucky for Walt, lucky for us.

clues.clue: Walt founded the studio in 1923 with this older brother, who handled the money.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Roy O. Disney. Walt dreamed it, Roy figured out how to pay for it. [chuckles] Every family needs a Roy.

clues.clue: This animator, Walt's longtime partner, did most of the original drawing of Mickey Mouse.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Ub Iwerks! [excited] He reportedly drew around 700 drawings a day for Plane Crazy. My hand hurts just thinking about it.

clues.clue: In 2006, Disney got the rights to Oswald back from NBCUniversal in a trade that sent this sportscaster to NBC.
clues.reveal: [laughs] The correct answer is Al Michaels! A rabbit traded for a play-by-play legend. Easily the weirdest trade in sports history.

categories.title: Original Attractions
categories.intro: [excited] It's PICTURE time! Every photo shows something that has been at Disneyland since its very first summer, 1955. Name what you see.

art.prompt: 16:9 card art: a sunny 1955-style amusement park midway seen from above: a white paddle-wheel riverboat on a river, a jeweled carousel, tiny vintage race cars on a winding track, and a pink castle in the distance, nostalgic postcard style No people, no recognizable characters, no text or logos.

clues.clue: This castle has stood at the end of Main Street, U.S.A. since Disneyland opened in 1955. Name it.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Sleeping Beauty Castle. And it has a real working drawbridge! [whispers] It has only been lowered twice.

clues.clue: This paddle-wheeler has cruised the Rivers of America since 1955. Name it.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Mark Twain Riverboat. Walt and Lillian kicked off their 30th anniversary party aboard it, four days before opening. [chuckles] Full steam ahead.

clues.clue: This Fantasyland ride, with its jumping horses, has been spinning at Disneyland since 1955. Name it.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is King Arthur Carrousel. Walt loved watching his daughters ride carousels, and that is part of how Disneyland was born. [sighs] Sweet.

clues.clue: Tomorrowland guests have been driving these little cars since opening day in 1955. Name the attraction.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Autopia! Back in 1955, kids got a taste of the brand new freeway life. Today it is the only ride where your little brother is allowed to drive.

clues.clue: This little Fantasyland train has chugged around Disneyland since the park's first summer of 1955. Its engine comes from what 1941 film?
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Dumbo! That is the Casey Junior Circus Train. [chuckles] I think I can, I think I can... name the movie.

categories.title: Dateline: 1955
categories.intro: [dramatic] Picture it. July 17th, 1955. Orange groves, fresh paint, and a dream about to open its gates. This category is all about Disneyland's opening.

art.prompt: 16:9 card art: a 1955 newspaper-style scene without any lettering: a golden ribbon across ornate park gates, orange groves on the horizon, vintage TV cameras on tripods, balloons drifting into a blue California sky No people, no recognizable characters, no text or logos.

clues.clue: Disneyland opened in 1955 in this sunny U.S. state.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is California! Florida got its turn in 1971. [laughs] Walt liked his parks the way he liked his oranges... sunny.

clues.clue: Disneyland's famous nickname is The ___ Place on Earth. Fill in the blank, then name the whole thing.
choices: The Most Magical Place on Earth
clues.reveal: The correct answer is The Happiest Place on Earth. The Most Magical Place on Earth? That's Walt Disney World. [chuckles] Do not mix them up at a family reunion.

clues.clue: Opening day was broadcast live on TV, and this future U.S. president was one of the hosts.
clues.reveal: [gasps] The correct answer is Ronald Reagan! He co-hosted with Art Linkletter and Bob Cummings, and some 90 million viewers may have tuned in.

clues.clue: On a scorching opening day, women's high heels sank into this freshly poured Main Street surface.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is asphalt. [sighs] The day got nicknamed Black Sunday. Overcrowding, broken fountains, sticky streets. And yet... look at it now.

clues.clue: Walt's private Disneyland apartment sits above this Main Street building, and a lamp stays lit in its window in his honor.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Fire Station. [whispers] When the lamp was on, cast members knew Walt was home. It still glows today.

categories.title: Walt-er Cooler Talk
categories.intro: [chuckles] Gather 'round the Walt-er cooler. This fan category is all about the man himself. Get it? Walt-er. [laughs] I'll be here all week.

art.prompt: 16:9 card art: a cozy 1950s office with a model steam locomotive on a desk, a framed farm landscape painting, an oval office water cooler, a fedora on a coat rack and a wall of golden trophy statuettes glowing softly No people, no recognizable characters, no text or logos.

clues.clue: Walt Disney was born in 1901 in this big Illinois city, home of the Cubs and the Bears.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Chicago! Walt was born there on December 5th, 1901. [excited] Deep dish and Disney, what a combo.

clues.clue: Walt's middle name, which he shared with his father.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Elias. Walter Elias Disney. [chuckles] Fancy.

clues.clue: This small Missouri farm town where Walt spent part of his childhood is said to have inspired Main Street, U.S.A.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Marceline, Missouri. Walt said more things happened to him there than in any other town. [sighs] Heartwarming.

clues.clue: Walt built a backyard railroad, the Carolwood Pacific. His locomotive was named after his wife Lillian. Name the engine.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Lilly Belle! And the name lives on in a fancy parlor car on the Disneyland Railroad. Choo choo!

clues.clue: Walt holds the record for the most competitive Academy Awards won by one person. How many?
clues.reveal: The correct answer is 22! Add in his honorary awards and it goes even higher. [laughs] At some point you need a bigger shelf.
